command:
set +e
set -uo pipefail
cd /tmp

# spawn runs --command/task commands under bash -e and `set -uo pipefail` does not clear it
# (spawn#707), so errexit is disabled above and every status is checked by hand.

IDX=mpa_vJun23_CHOCOPhlAnSGB_202403
MD5=d985de75a217cd319e721863f68e7d33
HOST=https://cmprod1.cibio.unitn.it/biobakery4/metaphlan_databases

echo "== fetch the index in-region rather than through someone's laptop =="
# MetaPhlAn's own hardcoded URL is http:// and 301s to https, so follow redirects.
# 3.32 GB: smaller than several inputs this catalog already stages (bwa-mem2's is 17.7 GB).
T0=$(date +%s)
curl -fL --no-progress-meter --retry 3 --retry-delay 5 -o "$IDX.tar" "$HOST/$IDX.tar"
RC=$?; T1=$(date +%s)
echo "curl_rc	$RC"
test "$RC" = "0" || { echo "download failed"; exit 1; }
BYTES=$(stat -c%s "$IDX.tar")
echo "download_s	$(( T1 - T0 ))"
echo "bytes	$BYTES"
printf 'MB_per_s	%.1f\n' "$(awk -v b=$BYTES -v s=$((T1-T0)) 'BEGIN{if(s>0)print b/1e6/s; else print 0}')"

echo "== verify against the md5 the DEPOSITORS publish next to the tarball =="
# This is the source's own integrity statement, which is what makes a tier-3 HTTP host
# acceptable: the bytes are checkable at the source, not merely checkable against ourselves.
echo "$MD5  $IDX.tar" > want.md5
md5sum -c want.md5 || { echo "published md5 does not match -- do NOT stage these bytes"; exit 1; }
echo "md5	matches the published $MD5"

echo "== our own sha256, which is what the recipe pins =="
sha256sum "$IDX.tar" | tee "$IDX.tar.sha256"

echo "== what is actually inside =="
tar -tf "$IDX.tar" | head -12
echo "entries	$(tar -tf "$IDX.tar" | wc -l)"
# This tar is the MARKER SET, not a built bowtie2 index -- MetaPhlAn runs bowtie2-build on
# first use. Measured contents: the .pkl metadata, SGB and VSG marker FASTAs, VINFO.csv.
# The first version of this check looked for .bt2l files and failed the task AFTER a
# perfectly good md5-verified download, so the expectation is written out explicitly.
for want in "$IDX.pkl" "${IDX}_SGB.fna.bz2" "${IDX}_VSG.fna.bz2"; do
  tar -tf "$IDX.tar" | grep -qx "$want" || { echo "missing $want from the tar"; exit 1; }
done
echo "markers	pkl + SGB + VSG present (bowtie2 index is BUILT, not shipped)"

echo "== stage =="
# No copy: /tmp is a tmpfs at half the instance RAM, so duplicating a 3.32 GB tar would
# cost 6.6 GB of it for nothing. The outputs name the file directly.
df -h /tmp | awk 'NR==2{print "  tmpfs\t"$2" total, "$4" free"}'
echo "== the version string HUMAnN parses, with NO database present =="
# HUMAnN reads `metaphlan --version` last line, column 2. MetaPhlAn appends a no-database
# warning there, so HUMAnN parses the word "MetaPhlAn" as a version and dies. Captured here
# because staging this index is what makes that warning go away.
metaphlan --version 2>&1 | sed 's/^/  ver_nodb\t/' | tail -4
echo "STAGE OK"
